When one cultivates the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, entering and abiding in the second jhána, which is without initial application, with only sustained application, born of concentration, and accompanied by zest and happiness, with earth kasiṇa as object, at that time there is contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, sustained application, zest, happiness, one-pointedness of mind, faculty of faith, faculty of energy, faculty of mindfulness, faculty of concentration, faculty of wisdom, mind faculty, faculty of joy, life faculty, right view, right effort...pe...exertion, non-distraction; and whatever other immaterial phenomena are dependently arisen at that time – these states are wholesome...pe....
At that time there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements, three nutriments, eight faculties, four jhāna factors, four path factors, seven powers, three roots, one contact...pe...one dhamma base, one dhamma element; and whatever other immaterial phenomena are dependently arisen at that time – these states are wholesome...pe....

When, at that time, due to wholesome kamma wrought and stored up in the sense sphere, a resultant mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity has arisen, apprehending a visible object or a mental object or whatever else, at that time, there is contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, initial application, sustained application, equanimity, one-pointedness of mind, mind faculty, equanimity faculty, life faculty; whatever other immaterial phenomena are dependently arisen at that time – these phenomena are indeterminate.

content: What is contact at that time? That which at that time is contact, touching, contacting, the state of having contacted – this is contact at that time.

content: What is feeling at that time? When one cultivates supramundane jhāna, leading to liberation, leading to cessation of accumulation, for the abandonment of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage of awakening, by the cessation of initial and sustained application... the second jhāna... the third jhāna... the fourth jhāna... the first jhāna... the fifth jhāna, entering and abiding with desireless, dominated by desire, these are wholesome... desireless, dominated by desire, these are resultant... desireless, dominated by desire, these are wholesome... signless, dominated by desire, these are resultant... desireless, dominated by desire, these are wholesome... emptiness, dominated by desire, these are resultant, at that time, contact... non-distraction... these states are indeterminate.

content: Which states are indeterminate?⤵When, as the result of unwholesome kamma having been wrought, having been stored up, eye-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, having visible form as its object; ear-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, having sound as its object; nose-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, having smell as its object; tongue-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, having taste as its object; body-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by pain, having tangible object as its object, then at that time there is contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, pain, one-pointedness of mind, mind faculty, pain faculty, life faculty; or whatever other immaterial phenomena there are at that time, arisen dependently – these phenomena are indeterminate.

content: The compilation of material phenomena is twofold –
source_content:
The compilation of material phenomena is twofold –
There is matter that is grasped; there is matter that is not grasped.
There is matter that is kammically acquired; there is matter that is not kammically acquired.
There is matter that is kammically acquired and an object of clinging; there is matter that is not kammically acquired and not an object of clinging.
There is matter that is visible; there is matter that is invisible.
There is matter with impact; there is matter without impact.
There is matter that is a faculty; there is matter that is not a faculty.
There is matter that is a great element; there is matter that is not a great element.
There is communicative matter, there is non-communicative matter.
There is mind-originated matter, there is not mind-originated matter.
There is matter conascent with mind, there is matter not conascent with mind.
There is matter following the mind, there is matter not following the mind.
There is internal matter, there is external matter.
There is gross matter, there is subtle matter.
There is far matter, there is near matter.
There is matter that is a base for eye-contact, there is matter that is not a base for eye-contact. There is matter that is a base for feeling born of eye-contact, for perception, for volition, for eye-consciousness; there is matter that is not a base for eye-consciousness.
There is matter that is a base for ear-contact, for nose-contact, for tongue-contact, for body-contact; there is matter that is not a base for body-contact. There is matter that is a base for feeling born of body-contact, for perception, for volition, for body-consciousness; there is matter that is not a base for body-consciousness.
There is matter that is an object for eye-contact, there is matter that is not an object for eye-contact. There is matter that is an object for feeling born of eye-contact, for perception, for volition, for eye-consciousness; there is matter that is not an object for eye-consciousness.
There is material form which is an object of ear-contact, and so on, up to body-contact; there is material form which is not an object of body-contact. There is material form which is an object of feeling arisen from body-contact, and so on, up to body-consciousness; there is material form which is not an object of body-consciousness.
There is material form which is the eye-base, and there is material form which is not the eye-base. There is material form which is the ear-base, and so on, up to the body-base; there is material form which is not the body-base.
There is material form which is the visible-form-base, and there is material form which is not the visible-form-base. There is material form which is the sound-base, and so on, up to the tangible-base; there is material form which is not the tangible-base.

content: What is that materiality which is the eye-base? ⤵That eye, which is a sensitivity derived from the four great primary elements, included within one's own being, invisible, and impinging; ⤵by which eye, invisible and impinging, one has seen, sees, will see, or may see visible and impinging matter. ⤵This is the eye, this is the eye-base, this is the eye element, this is the eye faculty, this is the world, this is a door, this is an ocean, this is lucent, this is a field, this is a base, this is a guide, this is sight, this is the hither shore, this is an empty village – ⤵this is that materiality which is the eye-base.
source_content:
What is that materiality which is the eye-base?
That eye, which is a sensitivity derived from the four great primary elements, included within one's own being, invisible, and impinging;
by which eye, invisible and impinging, one has seen, sees, will see, or may see visible and impinging matter.

content: What is edible food? Rice, gruel, flour, fish, meat, milk, curd, ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, molasses, or whatever other matter exists in any country, which is put into the mouth, chewed by the teeth, swallowed down the throat, filling the stomach, by the nutrient essence of which beings subsist—this is edible food.

The three wholesome roots—non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with them; and the bodily kamma, verbal kamma, and mental kamma arisen from them—these phenomena are wholesome.
source_content: Which phenomena are wholesome? The three wholesome roots—non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with them; and the bodily kamma, verbal kamma, and mental kamma arisen from them—these phenomena are wholesome.

content: Which phenomena are unwholesome? The three unwholesome roots—greed, hatred, delusion; and the defilements co-existent with them; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with them; and the bodily kamma, verbal kamma, and mental kamma arisen from them—these phenomena are unwholesome.
source_content: Which phenomena are unwholesome? The three unwholesome roots—greed, hatred, delusion; and the defilements co-existent with them; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with them; and the bodily kamma, verbal kamma, and mental kamma arisen from them—these phenomena are unwholesome.

content: Which phenomena are indeterminate? The resultants of wholesome and unwholesome phenomena in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate; and those functional phenomena that are neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor kamma-resultants; and all matter, and the unconditioned element—these phenomena are indeterminate.
source_content: Which phenomena are indeterminate? The resultants of wholesome and unwholesome phenomena in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane; the feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate; and those functional phenomena that are neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor kamma-resultants; and all matter, and the unconditioned element—these phenomena are indeterminate.

content: Which phenomena are associated with pleasant feeling? In the plane of pleasant feeling, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and supramundane, excluding pleasant feeling; the perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with it—these phenomena are associated with pleasant feeling.
source_content: Which phenomena are associated with pleasant feeling? In the plane of pleasant feeling, in the sense sphere, fine-material sphere, and supramundane, excluding pleasant feeling; the perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with it—these phenomena are associated with pleasant feeling.

content: Which phenomena are associated with painful feeling? In the plane of painful feeling, in the sense sphere, excluding painful feeling; the perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with it—these phenomena are associated with painful feeling.
source_content: Which phenomena are associated with painful feeling? In the plane of painful feeling, in the sense sphere, excluding painful feeling; the perception aggregate, formation aggregate, and consciousness aggregate associated with it—these phenomena are associated with painful feeling.

content: Which phenomena are associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?⤵The aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness, in the sense, fine-material, immaterial, and transcendent spheres, associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, excluding the feeling itself.
source_content:
Which phenomena are associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?
The aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness, in the sense, fine-material, immaterial, and transcendent spheres, associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, excluding the feeling itself.

content: Which phenomena are results?⤵The results of wholesome and unwholesome phenomena in the sense, fine-material, immaterial, and transcendent spheres, namely, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.
source_content:
Which phenomena are results?

Which phenomena have the nature of producing results?

content: Which phenomena are neither results nor having the nature of producing results?⤵Functional phenomena that are neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not kamma-results; all material phenomena; and the unconditioned element.

content: Which phenomena are not clung to, but graspable?⤵Wholesome and unwholesome phenomena, subject to taints, in the sense, fine-material, and immaterial spheres, namely, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness; functional phenomena that are neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not kamma-results; and matter not born of kamma.

content: Which phenomena are undefiled but defiling?⤵Wholesome and indeterminate phenomena, subject to taints, in the sense, fine-material, and immaterial spheres, namely, the aggregate of matter, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.

These phenomena are accompanied by initial application and sustained application.

These phenomena are accompanied by initial application and sustained application.

content: Which phenomena are without initial application, only sustained application?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate, associated with them, in the sphere of only sustained application (fine-material sphere and supramundane), excluding sustained application. These phenomena are without initial application, only sustained application.

The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate, associated with them, in the sphere of only sustained application (fine-material sphere and supramundane), excluding sustained application. content: Which phenomena are without initial application and without sustained application?⤵The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional formations aggregate, and consciousness aggregate, in the sphere without initial and sustained application (sense sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane); all material phenomena; and the unconditioned element. These phenomena are without initial application and without sustained application.

These phenomena are accompanied by joy.

Which phenomena are accompanied by joy?

content: Which phenomena are to be abandoned by vision?⤵The three fetters: personality view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals.
source_content:
Which phenomena are to be abandoned by vision?
The three fetters: personality view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals.

content: What is personality view?⤵Here, an uninstructed worldling, not seeing noble ones, unskilled in the Dhamma of noble ones, untrained in the Dhamma of noble ones; not seeing good men, unskilled in the Dhamma of good men, untrained in the Dhamma of good men, regards form as self, or self as having form, or form as in self, or self as in form; regards feeling as self, or self as having feeling, or feeling as in self, or self as in feeling; regards perception as self, or self as having perception, or perception as in self, or self as in perception; regards volitional formations as self, or self as having volitional formations, or volitional formations as in self, or self as in volitional formations; regards consciousness as self, or self as having consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Whatever such view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, distortion of views, vacillation of views, fetter of views, grasping, clinging, adherence, obsession, wrong path, false way, wrongness, sectarian position, inverted grasp – this is called personality view.
source_content:
What is personality view?
Here, an uninstructed worldling, not seeing noble ones, unskilled in the Dhamma of noble ones, untrained in the Dhamma of noble ones; not seeing good men, unskilled in the Dhamma of good men, untrained in the Dhamma of good men, regards form as self, or self as having form, or form as in self, or self as in form; regards feeling as self, or self as having feeling, or feeling as in self, or self as in feeling; regards perception as self, or self as having perception, or perception as in self, or self as in perception; regards volitional formations as self, or self as having volitional formations, or volitional formations as in self, or self as in volitional formations; regards consciousness as self, or self as having consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Whatever such view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, distortion of views, vacillation of views, fetter of views, grasping, clinging, adherence, obsession, wrong path, false way, wrongness, sectarian position, inverted grasp – this is called personality view.

content: What is doubt?⤵Doubts, is perplexed about, the Teacher; doubts, is perplexed about, the Dhamma; doubts, is perplexed about, the Saṅgha; doubts, is perplexed about, the training; doubts, is perplexed about, the past; doubts, is perplexed about, the future; doubts, is perplexed about, both past and future; doubts, is perplexed about, dependent arising and dependently arisen phenomena. Whatever such wavering, state of wavering, perplexity, doubt, two-way path, uncertainty, grasping at many sides, vacillation, wandering, lack of penetration, stiffness of mind, mental defilement – this is called doubt.
source_content:
What is doubt?
Doubts, is perplexed about, the Teacher; doubts, is perplexed about, the Dhamma; doubts, is perplexed about, the Saṅgha; doubts, is perplexed about, the training; doubts, is perplexed about, the past; doubts, is perplexed about, the future; doubts, is perplexed about, both past and future; doubts, is perplexed about, dependent arising and dependently arisen phenomena. Whatever such wavering, state of wavering, perplexity, doubt, two-way path, uncertainty, grasping at many sides, vacillation, wandering, lack of penetration, stiffness of mind, mental defilement – this is called doubt.

content: What is adherence to rites and rituals?⤵Among recluses and brahmins outside this doctrine, the view 'purification by virtue, purification by rites, purification by virtue and rites'. Whatever such view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, distortion of views, vacillation of views, fetter of views, grasping, clinging, adherence, obsession, wrong path, false way, wrongness, sectarian position, inverted grasp – this is called adherence to rites and rituals.
source_content:
What is adherence to rites and rituals?
Among recluses and brahmins outside this doctrine, the view 'purification by virtue, purification by rites, purification by virtue and rites'. Whatever such view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, distortion of views, vacillation of views, fetter of views, grasping, clinging, adherence, obsession, wrong path, false way, wrongness, sectarian position, inverted grasp – this is called adherence to rites and rituals.

content: Which are the states rooted in the Path? For one endowed with the Noble Path, the feeling aggregate up to the consciousness aggregate associated with the path factors (excluding the path factors themselves) are states rooted in the Path. For one endowed with the Noble Path, right view is both path and root; the feeling aggregate up to the consciousness aggregate associated with it (excluding right view itself) are states rooted in the Path. For one endowed with the Noble Path, non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion are the roots of the Path; the feeling aggregate up to the consciousness aggregate associated with them are states rooted in the Path.

These dhammas are capable of arising.

content: What is hatred? Resentment arises thinking: "He harmed me," "He is harming me," "He will harm me." Or thinking: "He harmed my dear and beloved one," "He is harming my dear and beloved one," "He will harm my dear and beloved one." Or thinking: "He benefited my disliked and unloved one," "He is benefiting my disliked and unloved one," "He will benefit my disliked and unloved one." Or resentment arises without reason. This mental resentment, repugnance, opposition, anger, wrath, ill-will, mental corruption, displeasure of mind, fury, fierceness, lack of satisfaction of mind—this is called hatred.

content: Which are the states that are cankers? Four cankers – the canker of sensual desire, the canker of existence, the canker of views, and the canker of ignorance.

content: Therein, what is the canker of sensual desire? That desire, lust, delight, craving, affection, torment, infatuation, and clinging for sensual objects – this is called the canker of sensual desire.

content: Therein, what is the canker of existence? That desire, lust, delight, craving, affection, torment, infatuation, and clinging for existence – this is called the canker of existence.

content: Therein, what is the canker of views? Whether the world is eternal, or not eternal, or finite, or infinite, or the soul is the same as the body, or different from the body, or a Tathagata exists after death, or does not exist, or both exists and does not exist, or neither exists nor does not exist after death; whatever such view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, perversion of views, agitation of views, fetter of views, grasping, adherence, dogmatic belief, perverted grasping, wrong path, false way, wrongness, heretical ground, perverted grasping – this is called the canker of views. All wrong views are the canker of views.

content: Therein, what is the canker of ignorance? Ignorance of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path to its cessation; ignorance of the past, of the future, of both, and of dependent arising in conditionally arisen phenomena; whatever such ignorance, non-seeing, non-comprehension, non-understanding, non-awakening, non-penetration, non-grasping, non-fathoming, non-reflection, non-reviewing, non-direct knowledge, dullness, folly, non-discernment, delusion, utter delusion, confusion, ignorance, flood of ignorance, bond of ignorance, latent disposition of ignorance, obsession of ignorance, chain of ignorance, delusion, root of unwholesome – this is called the canker of ignorance.

content: What is the Fetter of aversion?⤵Resentment arises thinking: 'He harmed me,' 'He is harming me,' 'He will harm me'; or similar thoughts regarding dear ones or disliked ones; or resentment arises without reason. Such mental resentment, opposition, aversion, hostility, anger, hatred, mental affliction, wrath, malice, enmity, fierceness, mental displeasure. This is called the Fetter of aversion.

content: Which states are bodily ties? There are four bodily ties: the bodily tie of covetousness, the bodily tie of ill will, the bodily tie of adherence to rites and rituals, the bodily tie of dogmatic adherence to "this is the truth".

content:
Among these, what is the bodily tie of covetousness? That which is lust, attachment, desire, craving, clinging, covetousness, greed, the root of unwholesomeness, a flood, a bond, a tie, a hindrance, a latent disposition, the root of suffering, Mara's snare
—this is called the bodily tie of covetousness.

content:
Among these, what is the bodily tie of ill will? Resentment arises, thinking: "He harmed me," "He is harming me," "He will harm me." Resentment arises, thinking: "He harmed my dear, beloved one," "He is harming my dear, beloved one," "He will harm my dear, beloved one." Resentment arises, thinking: "He benefited my disliked, unloved one," "He is benefiting my disliked, unloved one," "He will benefit my disliked, unloved one." Or resentment arises without a reason. That such resentment, repulsion, hatred, ill will, anger, displeasure of mind
—this is called the bodily tie of ill will.

—this is called the bodily tie of adherence to rites and rituals.

content: Therein, what is the hindrance of sensual desire? Whatever sensual desire for sense objects, sensual lust, sensual delight, sensual craving, sensual affection, sensual burning, sensual infatuation, sensual clinging – this is called the hindrance of sensual desire.

content: Therein, what is the hindrance of ill will? "He acted to my detriment" – ill will arises; "He is acting to my detriment" – ill will arises; "He will act to my detriment" – ill will arises. Similarly, ill will arises concerning the detriment of a loved and desirable one, or the benefit of an unloved and undesirable one. Or ill will arises groundlessly. Whatever such ill will of mind, resentment, aversion, opposition, anger, intense anger, complete anger, hatred, malice, complete malice, mental affliction, mental defilement, wrath, being angry, state of being angry, hostility, state of being hostile, malevolence, state of being malevolent, enmity, fierceness, ill-temper, displeasure of mind – this is called the hindrance of ill will.

content: Therein, what is sloth? Whatever mental unreadiness, unwieldiness, sinking, drooping, sluggishness, languor, state of being languid, sloth, state of being slothful – this is called sloth.

content: Among these, what is sloth? That unsuitability of the body, unworkability, being weighed down, enveloped, internally obstructed, sleepiness, drowsiness, the act of sleeping, the state of having slept – this is called sloth. Thus, this torpor and this sloth – this is called the hindrance of sloth and torpor.

content: Among these, what is worry? Such worry, worrying, the state of having worried, mental regret, mental defilement – this is called worry. Thus, this restlessness and this worry – this is called the hindrance of restlessness and worry.

content: Among these, what is the hindrance of skeptical doubt? Doubts and is uncertain about the Teacher, the Dhamma, the Sangha, the training, the past, the future, both past and future, and dependent arising and its conditionally arisen phenomena. Such doubt, doubting, the state of having doubted, perplexity, uncertainty, being of two minds, vacillation, indecision, inability to penetrate, mental rigidity, mental defilement – this is called the hindrance of skeptical doubt.

content: Section on Clinging
source_content: Section on Clinging

content: Which phenomena are clingings? Four clingings: sensual clinging, clinging to views, clinging to rites and rituals, clinging to a doctrine of self.
source_content: Which phenomena are clingings? Four clingings: sensual clinging, clinging to views, clinging to rites and rituals, clinging to a doctrine of self.

content: What is sensual clinging? That desire for sensual pleasures, lust for sensual pleasures, delight in sensual pleasures, craving for sensual pleasures, affection for sensual pleasures, agitation due to sensual pleasures, infatuation with sensual pleasures, obsession with sensual pleasures – this is called sensual clinging.
source_content: What is sensual clinging? That desire for sensual pleasures, lust for sensual pleasures, delight in sensual pleasures, craving for sensual pleasures, affection for sensual pleasures, agitation due to sensual pleasures, infatuation with sensual pleasures, obsession with sensual pleasures – this is called sensual clinging.

content: What is clinging to views? The view that there is no giving, no offering, no sacrifice; no fruit or result of good and bad actions; no this world, no other world; no mother, no father; no spontaneously born beings; no recluses and brahmins in the world who are rightly gone, rightly practiced, who have themselves realized and proclaimed this world and the other world by direct knowledge – such a view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, agitation of views, fickleness of views, fetter of views, grasp, holding, adherence, clinging, wrong path, false way, wrongness, heretical tenet, perverse grasp – this is called clinging to views. Excluding clinging to rites and rituals and clinging to a doctrine of self, all wrong views are clinging to views.

Excluding clinging to rites and rituals and clinging to a doctrine of self, all wrong views are clinging to views.

content: What is clinging to rites and rituals? Among recluses and brahmins outside [this dispensation], the view that purification is through virtue, purification is through vows, purification is through rites and rituals – such a view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, agitation of views, fickleness of views, fetter of views, grasp, holding, adherence, clinging, wrong path, false way, wrongness, heretical tenet, perverse grasp – this is called clinging to rites and rituals.

content: What is clinging to a doctrine of self? Here, an uninstructed worldling, not seeing noble ones, not skilled in the noble Dhamma, not trained in the noble Dhamma; not seeing true men, not skilled in the Dhamma of true men, not trained in the Dhamma of true men – perceives form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as being in self, or self as being in form. Feeling... perception... mental formations... consciousness he perceives as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as being in self, or self as being in consciousness. Such a view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, agitation of views, fickleness of views, fetter of views, grasp, holding, adherence, clinging, wrong path, false way, wrongness, heretical tenet, perverse grasp – this is called clinging to a doctrine of self.

source_content: What are defilements? The ten bases of defilements are: greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, skeptical doubt, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, and fearlessness of wrongdoing.

content: Therein, what is greed? That which is lust, attachment, desire, infatuation, clinging, covetousness; craving for sensuality, existence, non-existence, fine-material, immaterial, cessation, forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, mental objects; the flood, bond, knot, clinging, hindrance, latent disposition, root of suffering, covetousness, greed, the unwholesome root. This is called greed.
source_content: Therein, what is greed? That which is lust, attachment, desire, infatuation, clinging, covetousness; craving for sensuality, existence, non-existence, fine-material, immaterial, cessation, forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, mental objects; the flood, bond, knot, clinging, hindrance, latent disposition, root of suffering, covetousness, greed, the unwholesome root. This is called greed.

content: Therein, what is hatred? Ill-will arises concerning harm done to oneself or loved ones, or benefit to disliked ones, in the past, present, or future; or ill-will arises without reason. That which is such ill-will, aversion, opposition, anger, wrath, hatred, mental affliction, mental displeasure, fury, animosity, mental non-satisfaction. This is called hatred.

content: Therein, what is delusion? Ignorance of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path to its cessation; ignorance of the past, future, both past and future; ignorance of dependent arising and dependently arisen phenomena. That which is such ignorance, non-seeing, non-comprehension, dullness, foolishness, delusion, utter delusion, confusion, ignorance, flood of ignorance, bond of ignorance, latent disposition of ignorance, defilement of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root. This is called delusion.

content: Therein, what is conceit? Conceit thinking: 'I am superior,' 'I am equal,' 'I am inferior.' That which is such conceit, conceiving, elevation, upliftment, a banner, excessive grasping, desire for prominence of mind. This is called conceit.

content: Therein, what is wrong view? The view: 'The world is eternal,' or 'The world is not eternal,' or 'The world is finite,' or 'The world is infinite'; 'The soul is the same as the body,' or 'The soul is different from the body'; 'A Tathāgata exists after death,' or 'A Tathāgata does not exist after death,' or 'A Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,' or 'A Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.' That which is such view, wrong view, thicket of views, wilderness of views, contortion of views, vacillation of views, fetter of views, grasping, adherence, dogmatic belief, misapprehension, wrong path, wrongness, heretical ground, perverted grasping. This is called wrong view. All wrong views are (called) view.

content: Therein, what is skeptical doubt? Doubts and is uncertain about the Teacher, the Dhamma, the Saṅgha, the training; about the past, future, both past and future; about dependent arising and dependently arisen phenomena. That which is such doubt, wavering, uncertainty, perplexity, indecision, two-pronged path, uncertainty, hesitation, mental stiffness, mental defilement. This is called skeptical doubt.

content: Therein, what is shamelessness? That which is not being ashamed of what should be shameful, not being ashamed of committing evil, unwholesome actions. This is called shamelessness.

content: What is fearlessness of wrongdoing? Not dreading what should be dreaded, not dreading the committing of evil, unwholesome phenomena – this is called fearlessness of wrongdoing.

content: ⤵The Section on Abandonment.
source_content: ⤵The Section on Abandonment.

content: Which phenomena are to be abandoned by vision? The three fetters: identity view, doubt, and clinging to rites and rituals.
source_content: Which phenomena are to be abandoned by vision? The three fetters: identity view, doubt, and clinging to rites and rituals.

content: What is identity view? Here, an uninstructed ordinary person, not seeing the noble ones, unskilled in the noble Dhamma, undisciplined in the noble Dhamma, not seeing the true persons, unskilled in the Dhamma of the true persons, undisciplined in the Dhamma of the true persons, perceives form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. Feeling... perception... mental formations... consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Whatever such view, wrong view... up to... grasping of perversion – this is called identity view.

Feeling... perception... mental formations... consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. content: Among these, what is doubt? Wavering, doubting concerning the Teacher... stiffness of mind, mental defilement – this is called doubt.

content: Among these, what is clinging to rites and rituals? The view among recluses and brahmins outside [this dispensation] that purity comes from morality, purity comes from observances, purity comes from morality and observances – such a view, wrong view... mistaken apprehension – this is called clinging to rites and rituals. These three fetters, and defilements rooted in them, the feeling aggregate... consciousness aggregate associated with them, bodily action, vocal action, mental action originating from them – these states are to be abandoned by seeing.

content: What is skillfulness in dependent origination?⤵Ignorance conditions formations; formations condition consciousness; consciousness conditions mind-and-matter; mind-and-matter conditions the six sense bases; the six sense bases condition contact; contact conditions feeling; feeling conditions craving; craving conditions clinging; clinging conditions existence; existence conditions birth; birth conditions decay-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair. Thus arises this entire mass of suffering. That wisdom, understanding, non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, concerning this—this is called skillfulness in dependent origination.

content: What is unguardedness of the sense doors?⤵Here, perceiving forms with the eye, sounds with the ear, odors with the nose, flavors with the tongue, tangible objects with the body, or mental objects with the mind, one grasps at their general appearance and details. Whereby, while the respective faculty dwells unguarded, evil unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow in; one does not practice for its restraint, does not protect that faculty, does not undertake restraint in that faculty. The unguardedness, non-protection, non-guarding, non-restraint of these six faculties—this is called unguardedness of the sense doors.

content: What is moderation in food?⤵Here, some person, with reflection, skillfully takes food—not for sport, not for intoxication, not for adornment, not for beautification, but solely for the maintenance and continuance of this body, for the cessation of discomfort, for the support of the holy life. "Thus I will end old feelings and not produce new feelings, and there will be sustenance for me, blamelessness, and comfortable living." That satisfaction, moderation, reflection in food—this is called moderation in food.

That which is wisdom, understanding, non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called clear comprehension.

content: What is moral transgression? Bodily transgression, verbal transgression, or both bodily and verbal transgression. This is called moral transgression. All immorality is moral transgression.

content: What is wrong view?⤵There is no giving, no sacrifice, no offering; there is no fruit or result of good or evil deeds; there is no this world, nor the next; there is no mother, nor father; there are no spontaneously arisen beings; there are no recluses or brahmins in the world who have gone rightly, practiced rightly, who, having directly known and realized this world and the next by themselves, proclaim it. Such a view, wrong view...pe...perverted grasp. This is called wrong view. All wrong views are wrong view.

content: What is moral accomplishment? Bodily non-transgression, verbal non-transgression, or both bodily and verbal non-transgression. This is called moral accomplishment. All restraint in morality is moral accomplishment.

content:
What is accomplishment in view? There is what is given, offered, sacrificed; there is fruit and result of good and bad actions; there is this world, there is the other world; there is mother, there is father; there are spontaneously arisen beings; there are in the world ascetics and brahmins who are rightly gone and rightly practiced, who proclaim this world and the other world, having directly known and realized them themselves. Such wisdom, knowing... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view 
– this is called accomplishment in view. All right view is accomplishment in view.

content: Spiritual urgency is the fear of birth, the fear of old age, the fear of sickness, the fear of death. Grounds for spiritual urgency are birth, old age, sickness, death.

content: Proper exertion for one who has a sense of urgency: Here, a practitioner arouses desire, strives, exerts energy, grasps the mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states; for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states; for the arising of unarisen wholesome states; for the maintenance, non-forgetting, increase, development, cultivation, and perfection of arisen wholesome states.

content: Non-contentment with wholesome states is the desire for more for one not content with the cultivation of wholesome states.

content: Non-recoiling from exertion is diligent performance, continuous performance, unwavering performance, unflagging conduct, unabandoned desire, unabandoned burden in the repetition, development, and cultivation of wholesome states.

content: What phenomena are accompanied by initial application and sustained application? Wholesome and unwholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; eleven resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; two resultant unwholesome consciousnesses; eleven functional consciousnesses; the first fine-material jhána, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the first supramundane jhána, wholesome and resultant – excluding the initial application and sustained application arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by initial application and sustained application.

content: What phenomena are without initial application but with sustained application only? The second fine-material jhána in the five-fold system, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the second supramundane jhána in the five-fold system, wholesome and resultant – excluding the sustained application arising therein – and initial application – these phenomena are without initial application but with sustained application only.

content: What phenomena are without initial application and without sustained application? The two sets of fivefold sense consciousnesses; the fine-material jhána triads, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the four immaterial jhána consciousnesses, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the supramundane jhána triads, wholesome and resultant, and the second jhána in the five-fold system; and sustained application arising therein; and matter and Nibbána – these phenomena are without initial application and without sustained application. Sustained application co-arising with initial application should not be said to be accompanied by initial application and sustained application, nor only by sustained application, nor without initial application and without sustained application.

content: What phenomena are accompanied by rapture? Four wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses accompanied by joy; four unwholesome consciousnesses; five resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; five functional consciousnesses; the fine-material jhána dyads and triads, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the supramundane jhána dyads and triads, wholesome and resultant – excluding the rapture arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by rapture.

content: What phenomena are accompanied by happiness? Four wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses accompanied by joy; four unwholesome consciousnesses; six resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; five functional consciousnesses; the fine-material jhána triads and tetrads, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the supramundane jhána triads and tetrads, wholesome and resultant – excluding the happiness arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by happiness.

content: What phenomena are accompanied by equanimity? Four wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity; six unwholesome consciousnesses; ten resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; six resultant unwholesome consciousnesses; six functional consciousnesses; the fourth fine-material jhána, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the four immaterial jhána consciousnesses, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the fourth supramundane jhána, wholesome and resultant – excluding the equanimity arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by equanimity. Rapture is not accompanied by rapture, is accompanied by happiness, is not accompanied by equanimity. Happiness is not accompanied by happiness, may be accompanied by rapture, is not accompanied by equanimity, and may not be said to be accompanied by rapture. The two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, body-consciousness accompanied by pain, the feeling of equanimity, and matter and Nibbána – these phenomena should not be said to be accompanied by rapture, nor by happiness, nor by equanimity.

Rapture is not accompanied by rapture, is accompanied by happiness, is not accompanied by equanimity. Happiness is not accompanied by happiness, may be accompanied by rapture, is not accompanied by equanimity, and may not be said to be accompanied by rapture. The two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, body-consciousness accompanied by pain, the feeling of equanimity, and matter and Nibbána – these phenomena should not be said to be accompanied by rapture, nor by happiness, nor by equanimity.

content: What phenomena are to be abandoned by development? The consciousness accompanied by restlessness – these phenomena are to be abandoned by development. content: What dhammas have immeasurable objects? The four paths not included (in the realms), the four fruitions of recluseship – these dhammas have immeasurable objects. From wholesome sense-sphere consciousness, the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge; from functional consciousness, the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge; all unwholesome (consciousness) – these dhammas may have limited objects, may have exalted objects, not immeasurable objects, and may not be describable as having limited objects or as having exalted objects. From wholesome sense-sphere consciousness, the four consciousnesses associated with knowledge; from functional consciousness, the four consciousnesses associated with knowledge; the fourth rūpa-jhāna, both wholesome and functional; functional rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity – these dhammas may have limited objects, may have exalted objects, may have immeasurable objects, and may not be describable as having limited objects, or as having exalted objects, or as having immeasurable objects. The rūpa-jhānas of the triple and quadruple systems, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the resultant of the fourth jhāna; the base of infinite space; the base of nothingness – these dhammas are not describable as having limited objects, or as having exalted objects, or as having immeasurable objects. Matter and Nibbāna are without object.

content: What are the phenomena that are roots? The three wholesome roots, the three unwholesome roots, the three indeterminate roots. Non-greed is a wholesome root, non-hatred is a wholesome root, they arise in wholesome states in the four planes. Non-delusion is a wholesome root, it arises in wholesome states in the four planes, excluding the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge in sensuous wholesome states.⤵ Greed arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. Hatred arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure. Delusion arises in all unwholesome states.⤵ Non-greed is a resultant root, non-hatred is a resultant root, they arise in resultant states in the four planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous resultant. Non-delusion is a resultant root, it arises in resultant states in the four planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous resultant, and excluding the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge.⤵ Non-greed is a functional root, non-hatred is a functional root, they arise in functional states in the three planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous functional. Non-delusion is a functional root, it arises in functional states in the three planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous functional, and excluding the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge – these phenomena are roots.

Non-greed is a functional root, non-hatred is a functional root, they arise in functional states in the three planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous functional. Non-delusion is a functional root, it arises in functional states in the three planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous functional, and excluding the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge – these phenomena are roots.

content: What are the taints? The four taints: taint of sensual desire, taint of existence, taint of views, taint of ignorance. The taint of sensual desire arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. The taint of existence arises in the four consciousnesses accompanied by greed dissociated from wrong view. The taint of views arises in the four consciousnesses associated with wrong view. The taint of ignorance arises in all unwholesome states. These states are taints.

The taint of views arises in the four consciousnesses associated with wrong view. The taint of ignorance arises in all unwholesome states. These states are taints.

content: Which phenomena are fetters? The ten fetters: sensual craving, ill-will, conceit, wrong view, doubt, adherence to rites and rituals, craving for existence, envy, avarice, ignorance. Sensual craving arises in the eight greed-rooted consciousnesses. Ill-will arises in the two hate-rooted consciousnesses. Conceit arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses disjoined from wrong view. Wrong view arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses conjoined with wrong view. Doubt arises in the doubt-rooted consciousness. Adherence to rites and rituals arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses conjoined with wrong view. Craving for existence arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses disjoined from wrong view. Envy and avarice arise in the two hate-rooted consciousnesses. Ignorance arises in all unwholesome consciousnesses – these phenomena are fetters.

content: Which dhammas are ties? There are four ties: covetousness bodily tie, ill-will bodily tie, attachment to rites and rituals bodily tie, and dogmatic adherence to 'this is the truth' bodily tie. The covetousness bodily tie arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. The ill-will bodily tie arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure. The attachment to rites and rituals bodily tie and the dogmatic adherence to 'this is the truth' bodily tie arise in the four consciousnesses conjoined with wrong view – these dhammas are ties.

content: What are the phenomena that are hindrances? Six hindrances: sensual desire hindrance, ill will hindrance, sloth and torpor hindrance, restlessness and worry hindrance, skeptical doubt hindrance, ignorance hindrance. Sensual desire hindrance arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed; ill will hindrance arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure; sloth and torpor hindrance arises in prompted unwholesome states; restlessness hindrance arises in consciousnesses accompanied by restlessness; worry hindrance arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure; skeptical doubt hindrance arises in consciousnesses accompanied by skeptical doubt; ignorance hindrance arises in all unwholesome states. These phenomena are hindrances.

content: Which phenomena are clingings? The four clingings: sensual clinging, clinging to views, clinging to rites and rituals, clinging to a doctrine of self. Sensual clinging arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. Clinging to views, clinging to rites and rituals, and clinging to a doctrine of self arise in the four consciousnesses associated with wrong view – these phenomena are clingings.

content: The Section on Defilements
source_content: The Section on Defilements

content: What are defilements? The ten bases of defilements: greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, doubt, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, fearlessness of wrongdoing. Greed arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. Hatred arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure. Delusion arises in all unwholesome states. Conceit arises in the four consciousnesses accompanied by greed, dissociated from wrong view. Wrong view arises in the four consciousnesses associated with wrong view. Doubt arises in the consciousness accompanied by doubt. Sloth arises in prompted unwholesome states. Restlessness, shamelessness, and fearlessness of wrongdoing arise in all unwholesome states. These states are defilements.
